correctness.rationale: For each rook edge, the two squares form a unique two-edge path in K_{m,n}. Inducedness is exactly vertex-disjointness of these paths. Their row- and column-centered types, with a and b components and residual r=m-a-2b, c=n-2a-b, have count m!n!/(2^(a+b)a!b!r!c!). A packing is inclusion-maximal iff K_{r,c} admits no two-edge path, i.e. r=0 or c=0 or (r,c)=(1,1). Labeled exponential generating functions follow. Feasible size k is characterized by k<=m,n and 3k<=m+n; maximality lower bound ceil(min(m,n)/2) is attained by explicit row-saturating stars, with small cases treated. Equating the two extrema gives precisely nine unordered rectangles. Direct brute enumeration of every induced rook matching over all 16 boards 2<=m,n<=5 agrees in 6201 cases; algebraic coefficient checks cover 289 boards up to dimension 18. Finite tests are not used as proofs of the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The complete bivariate enumerators for induced and inclusion-maximal induced matchings in arbitrary rectangular rook graphs, their two extremal parameters, and the exact nine-shape well-indumatched classification are not supplied by the materially inspected nearest general articles or distinct-object enumeration table. The counting bijection explicitly treats equivalent disjoint P3-packings of K_{m,n}. Specialized earlier path-packing enumerations could still cover the result and are a material residual priority risk; absence of search hits is not itself proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A differently indexed formula enumerating all vertex-disjoint two-edge paths in arbitrary complete bipartite graphs might imply the first polynomial without using rook graph language.
An earlier full enumeration of maximal P3-packings in complete bipartite graphs could imply both generating functions and the classification.

value.rationale: The two complete cardinality distributions solve a natural enumeration and structural classification for induced, not ordinary, matchings of labeled rectangular rook graphs. The maximal subfamily requires an extra combinatorial condition not obtained merely from the usual labeled set formula; this yields the exact minimum and maximum maximal sizes and the sharp nine-board well-indumatched classification. The exact polynomial can benchmark algorithms and distinguish packing regimes. The 6x6 example has distinct maximal sizes 3 (3600) and 4 (8100), showing the classification detects genuine phenomena; this is more than an isolated small numerical improvement. Value is contingent on scientific novelty as compared with inspected literature, whose residual limitations are stated.
